messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: prod-serving cluster (us-west-2) - rapid autoscaler oscillation detected. Multiple GPU nodes spun up then reclaimed within ~5m. High pod restart rate with OOM and CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL logs. Pager sent to @alex.sre and @maya.runtime.

alex.sre: oncall here, starting triage. tagging thread.

maya.runtime: seeing repeated failures opening big KV cache regions during pod init. When scale-down hits mid-warm, pods lose GPU backing and trigger CUDA allocation errors + kernel driver complaints. Also noticed a few pods showing `cudaSetDevice` segfaults.

jing.infra: kube events snapshot: ```
Events:
  Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  5m   cluster-autoscaler  Scaled up rs/serving-xyz to 25
  Normal  ScaleDown           3m   cluster-autoscaler  Scale-down: removing 15 nodes
  Warning Eviction           3m   kubelet             Evicted pod serving-xyz due to memory pressure
  Warning Unhealthy          2m   kubelet             Liveness probe failed: read timeout
```

nora.cs: customer impact: elevated 5xx (about +14%), embeddings throughput reduced; multiple support tickets from big customers in us-west. CS needs status blurb and ETA.

sam.ops: dashboard: p50 +180ms, p95 +920ms, error rate delta +14.2% over baseline. Traffic shows short burst around the scale-up start.

maya.runtime: immediate plan: 1) disable scale-down / increase scale-down delay; 2) raise min replicas for serving to avoid full eviction of warm pods; 3) enable fallback routing to quantized-small model for non-paid or best-effort requests; 4) cordon nodes with suspect driver mismatches.

Commands I will apply now:```bash
# set scale-down delay to 15m
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment cluster-autoscaler --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/-","value":"--scale-down-delay=15m"}]'
# bump replicas to keep warmed caches
kubectl -n redwood scale deployment/serving --replicas=40
```

alex.sre: applying patches, will monitor logs for restarts.

incident-bot: scale-down delay patch submitted (job 9122).

Outputs:```
deployment.apps/cluster-autoscaler patched
deployment.apps/serving scaled
```

jing.infra: cloud provider console shows a flurry of preemptible reclaim events coincident with the autoscaler decisions. I'm marking provider-related terminations and opening a ticket with provider ops. Also cordoning 8 nodes that reported driver version mismatches.

maya.runtime: sample failing container log pre-mitigation:```
[2026-03-15T08:42:11Z] runtime init: allocating KV cache=1.5GB
E gpu: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E runtime: SIGABRT from cudaSetDevice
E kubelet: container exited with status 137
```

sam.ops: after mitigation metrics (10m): error delta down to +5.6%, p95 down to +300ms. Still degraded but improving. CS notified of interim update.

nora.cs: posting short note to customers: "We observed capacity instability in US-West affecting inference latency and error rates. We have paused aggressive scale-down behavior and increased warm replica counts. A smaller-model fallback is active for lower-priority requests. We expect service to stabilize within 20-40 minutes; we'll update if conditions change." :mailbox_with_mail:

alex.sre: next steps put here: - infra to reprovision cordoned nodes with validated driver images (jing) - runtime to add fast GPU-driver-check at pod start (maya) - ops to review autoscaler policy for bursty traffic (sam) - product/CS follow-up message (nora)

jing.infra: cordon+drain done for 8 nodes. reprovision in progress, ETA ~18m.

maya.runtime: temporary runtime tweak: add early exit on driver mismatch to avoid crashlooping and let scheduler pick healthy node. We'll follow up with a preflight binary that checks driver + cuda version before starting heavy allocs.

incident-bot: snapshot 20m post-mitigation: container_restarts -85%, 5xx delta +4.8%, p95 +260ms. Monitoring holds.

alex.sre: marking mitigated for now, leaving thread open for 1h. schedule retrospective in 48h to tune autoscaler stabilization window and fallback thresholds.

maya.runtime: hypothesis: autoscaler reacted to short burst (likely user job) causing scale-up; scale-down removed nodes during pod warmup causing eviction + driver mismatch cascades -> OOM/CUDA errors -> crashloops -> visible customer errors. Fixes: autoscaler hysteresis, keep-warm replicas, driver preflight, and model-fallback.

incident-bot: incident status: MITIGATED - monitoring. Thread will auto-close if stable. :white_check_mark:
